claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Replacing continuous-wave exposure with controlled pulsed-laser exposure and approximately 200 °C in-situ preheating reduces the peak thermal input to the powder.
Pulsed energy delivery produces a smaller, more spatially localized melt pool.
A smaller, localized melt pool promotes rapid solidification.
Rapid solidification under the proposed conditions refines the alloy microstructure.
In-situ preheating lowers the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding material.
Lowering the melt-pool temperature differential decreases thermal gradients.
Decreasing thermal gradients reduces residual thermal stress.
The proposed thermal regime reduces phase or microstructural degradation and better preserves the intended alloy structure.
Microstructural refinement under the proposed regime improves tensile properties relative to continuous-wave high-thermal-load processing.
Microstructural refinement under the proposed regime improves fatigue properties relative to continuous-wave high-thermal-load processing.
The proposed regime reduces residual stress relative to conventional continuous-wave processing.
The proposed regime minimizes or eliminates the need for post-processing heat treatments.
Pulse energies of approximately 50–150 mJ constitute an applicable processing window for the proposed process.
A build-chamber preheat temperature of approximately 200 °C is suitable for moderating thermal gradients.
The intervention is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components with volumes below approximately 1 cm³.
Conventional continuous-wave high-energy processing of AlCrFeNiSi is associated with large melt pools.
Conventional continuous-wave high-energy processing of AlCrFeNiSi is associated with high thermal gradients and significant residual stresses.
Conventional continuous-wave high-energy processing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Poorly optimized pulse parameters may introduce porosity.
